title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools Guide
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical Company Handbook entry for engineers and cross-functional teammates joining or working at Redwood Inference. It consolidates guidance on: roles and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and the primary internal tools and workflows you will use day-to-day.

Intended audience: all Redwood employees and new hires. Owners: People Ops (primary), Engineering Managers (careers), People Managers (onboarding).

Quick links
- Roles & career ladders section: see 'Roles & Career Ladders' below
- New hire checklist: see 'Hiring & Onboarding' section
- Internal tools cheat sheet: see 'Internal Tools Guide'

1) Roles & Career Ladders

Purpose
- Provide a clear leveling framework across Engineering, Product, and Research so employees understand expectations, promotion criteria, and typical career paths.

Overview of bands
- IC track: IC1 (New grad / Entry) -> IC2 -> IC3 -> Senior IC (IC4) -> Staff (IC5) -> Principal (IC6+)
- Manager track: Mgr1 (First-time manager) -> Mgr2 -> Director -> Senior Director
- Product & Research follow parallel ranges with role-specific competencies.

Role expectations (summary table)
| Band | Typical years | Core expectations | Example impact |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| IC2 | 1-3 | Delivers features with guidance; writes clear PRs; participates in design reviews | Owns small service or feature area |
| IC3 | 3-5 | Designs subsystems; mentors junior engineers; reliable on-call contributor | Leads cross-team project |
| IC4 (Senior) | 5+ | Shapes architecture; technical leadership; influences product direction | Owns major subsystem and roadmap |

Promotion criteria (common pillars)
- Technical quality: system design, code quality, reliability and performance improvements.
- Product & customer impact: shipping features with measurable outcomes (latency, cost, uptime, developer experience).
- Leadership & collaboration: mentoring, cross-team influence, proactive communication.
- Scope & autonomy: degree of independent ownership and decision-making.

Process
1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet: summary, 3-5 impact examples, recent performance feedback, and proposed new role responsibilities.
2. Manager reviews and provides written feedback.
3. Promotion committee (cross-functional) evaluates against ladder rubric and provides decision within two weeks.

Ownership and questions
- People Ops: process governance and calibration cadence
- Eng managers: write recommendations and coach candidates
- For questions: careers@redwood.com

2) Benefits & Perks

Core benefits (standard for all full-time employees)
- Health: employer-paid medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple tiers; HSA-compatible options.
- Financial: competitive base salary, equity grants (RSUs/options) at hire and refresh cycles, 401(k) with employer match.
- Time off: 20 days PTO baseline (pro-rated first year), company holidays, parental leave (primary/secondary), flexible remote work policy.
- Insurance & safety: Life & AD&D, short- and long-term disability.

Perks and allowances
- Learning & development stipend: $1,500/year for books, courses, conferences.
- Home office stipend: $500 one-time + ergonomic reimbursement up to $350.
- Wellness: monthly wellbeing stipend, on-site/partner gym discounts.
- Commuter: regional commuter benefits where applicable.

Equity and compensation cycles
- New hire equity grant communicated in offer letter.
- Compensation review cadence: annual performance cycle (Q1) with ad-hoc market adjustments as needed.

How to access benefits
- Benefits portal: benefits.redwood.com (login via Google Workspace)
- For claims and questions: benefits@redwood.com

3) Hiring & Onboarding Overview

Hiring philosophy
- Core values: hire for high technical standards, operational rigor for production inference, and strong collaboration skills.
- Interview process: phone screen -> technical take-home or paired design -> onsite (remote) loop -> final hire decision.

Interview loop (engineering, typical)
1. Recruiter screen (30 min): role fit, compensation guardrails, relocation/remote constraints.
2. Technical screen (45 min): systems or algorithms depending on level.
3. Pairing/design exercise (90 min): architecture, trade-offs, and telemetry considerations.
4. Cross-functional interview (60 min): product/ops alignment and communication.
5. Hiring committee review and offer.

Offer & acceptance
- Offers are issued by People Ops recruiting partner. Compensation, equity, start date and basic onboarding schedule are included.

New hire onboarding (first 90 days) — checklist
Pre-start (People Ops checklist)
- Send welcome packet and hardware survey.
- Provision access: Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, Okta, 1Password.
- Set up first-week meetings and buddy assignment.

Day 1-7
- Complete HR paperwork and benefits enrollment.
- Team onboarding session: architecture overview, key repos, on-call expectations.
- Security & compliance training (mandatory).

Week 2-4
- Small ramp project with mentor; pair programming sessions.
- Slack: introduce yourself in #team-{team-name}.
- Set 30/60/90 goals with manager.

Month 2-3
- Take ownership of a production issue or feature.
- Feedback checkpoint: manager + peer reviews.

Onboarding ownership
- People Ops: account provisioning and orientation logistics.
- Manager: role-specific onboarding, 1:1s, and performance expectations.
- Buddy: day-to-day help and social introduction.

4) Internal Tools Guide (cheat sheet)

Authentication & identity
- Okta: primary SSO provider for corporate apps. Always use MFA.
- 1Password: shared vaults for team secrets; use your assigned team vault and follow secret rotation policy.

Communication & async work
- Slack: primary messaging. Key channels: #all-company, #eng-platform, #sre-oncall, #team-{team-name}. Use threads for focused conversations.
- Email: Google Workspace for formal comms and external outreach.
- Confluence: canonical documentation lives here. Update pages when you ship changes to architecture or runbooks.

Code, CI/CD & deployment
- GitHub: monorepo and service repos. Use branch protection rules; PR templates are mandatory.
- CI: GitHub Actions for unit/integration tests; long-running perf tests run in the benchmarking pipeline.
- Deployment: Terraform + Spinnaker (or equivalent orchestration). Follow infra-standards before rolling changes.

Monitoring & on-call
- Datadog: metrics and dashboards. Standard SLO dashboards are under 'eng-sre'.
- PagerDuty: on-call routing for production incidents. Ensure you are enrolled and know the runbook for your service.
- Slack alerts: critical alerts post to #sre-oncall with clear remediation steps.

Observability & debugging tools
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry-based traces stored in Jaeger-compatible backend. Follow profiling-playbook for CPU/GPU hotspots.
- Logs: centralized ELK stack (or managed linear equivalent) with retention policies defined in 'data-residency-and-retention'.

How to request access or report issues
1. Submit access request via Okta access workflows (link in People Ops onboarding checklist).
2. For blocked access to repos/tools, file a support ticket in the internal IT queue (IT Helpdesk).
3. If you discover a missing doc or runbook gap, add a draft Confluence page and tag @people-ops and @eng-platform for review.

5) Routines and best practices
- Keep docs up to date: when you ship changes that affect operators or users, update Confluence and include a short changelog in the page.
- PRs: include test plan, rollout plan, and rollback steps for infra or runtime changes.
- Security: follow the secure-sdlc guidance; all PRs touching data handling must include a short security checklist.

Appendix: Useful templates and snippets
- New hire 30/60/90 goals template (copy in Confluence):
  - 30 days: Complete core training and small ramp task
  - 60 days: Ship a bug fix or small feature and own a service area
  - 90 days: Lead a retrospective and propose a service improvement

- Promotion packet checklist: summary, impact examples, metrics, manager letter, peer refs (3+), proposed role doc.

Contacts & escalation list
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- IT Helpdesk: it-helpdesk@redwood.com
- Security & Compliance: security@redwood.com
- Careers and promotions: careers@redwood.com

Maintenance & review cadence
- This handbook page owner: People Ops (primary).
- Review cadence: quarterly review and update or as policy changes.
- Last reviewed by: Alex Torres, Priya Patel on 2026-03-01

End of document.
